title: Recovering a one-bit function's value from its Fourier coefficients
statement:
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function of a single bit, and write $\hat f(\emptyset)$ and $\hat f(\{0\})$ for its two Fourier--Walsh coefficients, where $\{0\}$ is the singleton frequency consisting of the sole coordinate. Then the value of $f$ at the input whose coordinate is set (the bit value corresponding to $-1$ under the sign encoding) equals the difference of these two coefficients,
\[
  f(1) \;=\; \hat f(\emptyset) - \hat f(\{0\}).
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function of arity 1
replaced:
For a one-bit function $f$, its value on the all-$\mathit{true}$ input is the difference of
its two Fourier coefficients:
$f(\mathit{true}) = \widehat{f}(\emptyset) - \widehat{f}(\{0\})$.
